question: The ledger's commit gate is now permanently unsatisfiable, so the verified product work cannot be committed. Authorise the resolution surface, or conclude without committing?
why_now: Three finished slices are complete and independently verified but uncommitted: the Theme Studio moved into the shared shell (same URL, shell-owned, theme supplies only the content fragment), a 75% shell performance win (1.572s -> 0.390s per GET; 43 SELECTs and 43 prepared statements removed per request), and the shell spec repaired so every test fits the unchanged 30s budget. commit-check reports NOT ELIGIBLE with 24 blocking runs, and 22 of them cannot be cleared by any existing route. MEASURED: (1) 18 runs are status=completed with trust_surface_mismatch. trustSurfaceMismatch() compares each run's recorded hash against the CURRENT digest, so any later trust-surface edit invalidates all history; the designed remedy is .ai/trust-surface-amendments.json, which has 12 prior entries each carrying a director_decision (CD-28, CD-48, CD-51 ...). The current digest c40959a0888c73e91df5cc2a410192cbd5db37b9f725b5284ec94bc53099e9f4 is NOT amended, and no recorded decision covers the edit that moved it. (2) 2 runs are status=blocked and acknowledgeBlock() would accept them, but --director-decision must resolve to a recorded decision (^## REF in .ai/chair-decisions.md or .ai/decisions/REF.json) and none applies. (3) 4 runs are status=abandoned and have NO path at all: acknowledgeBlock() refuses anything that is not status==='blocked' && scope_conformance.ok===false; the only successor relief is in_array(status, ['failed','silent']) at line 2064; and start refuses a predecessor that is not failed/silent/completed-with-failed-verification, so an abandoned run cannot even be linked to a successor. decorateRun() adds only age. The gate is literally $blocking === [] ? EXIT_OK : EXIT_GATE. Therefore committing is impossible without changing verifier behaviour, which CD-21 rule 4 and the required_for_trust_surface convention reserve to the owner. The four abandoned records are my own duplicate dispatches that I killed, plus the option-A shell-spec run superseded by the approved option B; none is a live run, and none is writing to the tree.

options.label: Record the trust-surface amendment and acknowledge the two blocked runs, but change no verifier behaviour
options.effect: 20 of 24 blocks clear. The 4 abandoned runs still block, so commit-check stays NOT ELIGIBLE and the product remains uncommitted
options.cost: one amendment entry plus two acknowledgements; no code change

options.label: Extend the ledger's resolution surface so a terminal non-completed run can be closed by a recorded director decision, then amend and close all 24
options.effect: The commit gate becomes satisfiable again. All 24 clear, the product can be committed, and any future abandoned run is resolvable the same way. Every existing check is retained - the escape widens, the check does not weaken, and each use still requires a recorded director decision with a mandatory reason
options.cost: one bounded trust-surface edit, a new trust-surface amendment entry, and 24 recorded resolutions
options.blast_radius: verifier: every future commit could cite the widened escape, so it must record a decision reference and a reason per use
options.reversibility: reversible via the append-only record; runs are never mutated

options.label: Do not change the verifier; record the 24 blocks as a known limitation and do not commit
options.effect: No verifier change. The verified product work stays uncommitted and at risk, and the gate never reopens - every future slice adds blocks to a list that can only grow

recommendation.rationale: It is the only option that restores the objective. The other two leave the gate permanently unsatisfiable: option 'amend-and-acknowledge-only' clears 20 of 24 and still cannot commit, and option 'leave-the-gate-closed' guarantees that every future session accumulates more unresolvable blocks. It preserves every check, mutates no run, deletes no provenance, and still requires a recorded director decision with a mandatory reason for each resolution - so it widens the escape rather than weakening the gate. Recorded honestly: this is the one option that changes verifier behaviour, and if you judge that to be weakening in the sense of the absolute prohibition, then 'leave-the-gate-closed' is the compliant default and I will not perform the change.

impact_of_no_decision: The three verified slices stay uncommitted. Nothing else is blocked - verification, dispatch and the Akira roadmap all continue - but the completed product work remains at risk and the commit gate stays permanently closed.
already_done: Theme Studio moved into the shared shell, verified: npx playwright test tests/browser/akira-admin-shell.spec.ts passes, and the earlier akira-admin-shell spec passed 2/2 over real HTTP
Performance pass 1 and 2: 1.572s -> 0.390s per GET (-75%), 43 SELECTs and 43 prepared statements removed per request

Shell spec partition repair (option B, approved): full suite npx playwright test = 17 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped at the DEFAULT 30s timeout; 20 asserted routes on each viewport; 40 screenshots; playwright.config.js byte-identical at SHA-256 03ac0549c9bed0082da4e974a7f45c402ddf34a474fb1098ece918d1fb97eac3
Two independent verification runs of the shell spec: worst case 20.4s per test against the 30s budget (the repair lane reported 7.5s, which did not reproduce and is recorded as optimistic)

Root cause of the earlier red suite proved by measurement: assertNoSignOutCollision() made ~40 Playwright round-trips per call and was called twice per route at 600px; batching it into one nav.evaluate() removed 109.2s of the 126.4s spent in collision checks
